qs.q: A research team uses focus group discussions with homogeneous groups of twelve members. Why is group size restricted?
o: A. To ensure every participant has adequate speaking time.
B. To minimize logistical burdens on transcription equipment.
C. To comply strictly with national biometric privacy laws.
D. To reduce the financial stipend required for attendees.
E. To prevent statistical sampling errors in qualitative counts.
qs.e: Smaller group sizes ensure that all members can actively contribute during qualitative discussions.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Community Health Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: What distinguishes qualitative focus group discussions from quantitative community surveys?
o: Yielding numerical data suitable for statistical regression modeling.
Eliminating the requirement for trained qualitative moderators.
Requiring random sampling of entire regional populations.
Exploring underlying perceptions, motivations, and social norms.
Producing generalizable statistical prevalence rates for populations.
qs.e: Qualitative focus groups explore underlying perceptions, motivations, and social norms rather than numbers.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Community Health Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: During Step 3 of community diagnosis data collection, a researcher conducts a Focus Group Discussion (FGD). What is a defining structural characteristic of an FGD according to the study notes?
o: It collects strictly quantitative data using numerical scores
It involves heterogeneous groups to maximize debate
It consists of homogeneous groups with a maximum of 15 members
It requires a fixed minimum of 30 sessions per community
qs.e: Focus Group Discussions are qualitative methods that use homogeneous groups with a maximum of 15 people per group. The total number of groups is determined by data saturation.
qs.s: Community Health: Principles, Concepts & Diagnosis Guide: MCQs
